_how: Analyst commentary added after each investigation. {path|format} placeholders are filled from data/processed/findings.json by tools/health_report.py, so no number is typed by hand.
C02: The extra one-time codes of mid-September came from iPhone users on iOS 27 (all customers were affected). In that segment true mistaken matches reached {sim.e2.issue_ios27.true_fp_rate|.1%} while the confidence implied {sim.e2.issue_ios27.implied_fp_rate|.1%}: the score was overconfident and your step-up share on iOS 27 rose from {sim.e2.c02_step_up_share.after.ios27|.1%} (after the fix) to {sim.e2.c02_step_up_share.issue.ios27|.1%}. Fixed by the model release of {sim.e2.fix_date}; no action needed on your side.
C07: The visitor ids grouping hundreds of accounts (up to {sim.e3.accounts_per_visitor.all.max|,}) are {sim.e3.internal_rule.flagged} support-agent computers on shared office networks, correctly identified. Without internal traffic and robots, a visitor id carries {sim.e3.accounts_per_visitor.excl_internal_and_bots.mean|.2f} accounts on average and {sim.e3.accounts_per_visitor.excl_internal_and_bots.p99|.0f} at the 99th percentile (shared family devices). Recommendation: tag internal traffic.
C09: Private browsing went from {sim.e7.incognito_share_before|.0%} to {sim.e7.incognito_share_after|.0%} of your traffic after your campaign of {sim.e7.campaign_date}. Each kind of traffic is recognised as well as before; the overall error rate rises because the mix changed, and the measured rate stays flat ({sim.e7.measured_error_before|.1%} then {sim.e7.measured_error_after|.1%}) because private browsing cannot enter the control set. Read accuracy by traffic type.
P01: Between {sim.e6.wave.0} and {sim.e6.wave.1}, bad robots made up {sim.e6.bot_share_wave|.0%} of your requests (usual level {sim.e6.bot_share_outside|.1%}). They explain the jump of visitors per account ({sim.e6.visitors_per_account_wave_all|.2f} with robots, {sim.e6.visitors_per_account_wave_excl_bots|.2f} without). With flagged robots removed the false-negative rate is still {sim.e6.fn_humans_wave|.1%} (other weeks {sim.e6.fn_humans_outside|.1%}): the excess comes from robots that were not flagged. On genuinely human traffic (known here because the data is simulated) it was {sim.e6.fn_true_humans_wave|.1%}, against {sim.e6.fn_true_humans_outside|.1%} in other weeks. We recommend presenting human accuracy and robot detection as two separate results.
